correctness.rationale: Writing each triangular matrix by scalar c plus determinant-coordinate vector v=(a-c,b), the commutator vanishes iff det(v,w)=0; for every nonzero v, exactly q^2 scalar matrices map to it. Primitive vectors form q(q+1) projective points, each containing q^2-q unit generators, with determinant zero between distinct primitives exactly within one point. Nonprimitive nonzero vectors are the q^2-1 elements of m^2 minus zero, all mutually determinant-zero; each excludes exactly q of the q(q+1) primitive points over one residue-field direction. Choosing zero or one matrix per compatible primitive point yields first term; choosing one of q^2(q^2-1) nonprimitive matrix fibers leaves q^2 primitive points and yields second term. Since q^2+1<q(q+1) for q>=2, top degree and coefficient are exact. Reconstructed finite Z/4 graph type (15 nonzero vectors and four matrix lifts), exhaustively enumerated all 2^15 vector subsets with determinants mod 4; coefficients [1,60,1344,14848,86016,245760,262144] match polynomial, sum 610173. No infinite-q claim rests on enumeration.

value.rationale: PASS: The independence polynomial is the complete distribution of noncommuting matrix subsets for a natural finite-ring graph, not a renaming of its known independence number. The exact projective-line fiber decomposition, interaction with nilpotent directions, and universality across nonisomorphic length-two chain rings give meaningful previously unreported structural enumeration, potentially useful for finite ring graph invariants.

final_claim: For any finite commutative chain ring R with maximal ideal m !=0, m^2=0, |R/m|=q, the noncentral triangular-matrix commuting graph has independence polynomial (1+q^2(q^2-q)z)^(q(q+1))+q^2(q^2-1)z(1+q^2(q^2-q)z)^(q^2); alpha=q(q+1) and top coefficient (q^2(q^2-q))^(q(q+1)), independent of the ring isomorphism type.
limitations: Finite commutative chain rings of nilpotent maximal ideal of EXACT square-zero length two; all q prime powers.
Result concerns independent sets (pairwise noncommuting), not commuting cliques, central matrices, arbitrary nonprincipal local rings, or higher triangular matrix size.
Originality is best-of-knowledge; literature index coverage not exhaustive.
